subject: Clarification request: SOC 2 Type II coverage for phased migration / roll-forward policy
messages:
From: Security - FinBank <security@finbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — coverage window for phased migration

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as our SOC 2 team prepares their paperwork: we are confirming whether Redwood’s upcoming Type II report (period: 2026-01-01 through 2026-09-30) should be interpreted as inclusive of services that were migrated mid-period. Specifically:

- Our SaaS production traffic for the payments microservice was migrated from Redwood-hosted v1 to Redwood-managed v2 on 2026-05-17 at 23:45 UTC. The old instance received no traffic after that timestamp.
- Does Redwood treat that as a point-in-time snapshot (i.e., evidence must show the state at 2026-05-17 23:45) or as the new instance being part of the audit period from 2026-05-18 onwards (i.e., roll-forward evidence to show controls continued after cutover)?

We need to document this in our readiness notes and would like to know whether:
1) the Type II report and any bridge letter will explicitly call out mid-period phased migrations, and
2) if Redwood provides guidance on what evidence (snapshots, config exports, KV-cache manifests, traffic logs) satisfies auditors for a cutover day.

Appreciate a short note and any sample artifacts you can share so we can align our auditor’s expectations.

Thanks,
Marcus Liu
Security Engineer, FinBank
security@finbank.com

[Attachment: finbank-service-map.pdf (reference)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Security - FinBank <security@finbank.com>
Cc: lauren_bennett <lauren@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — coverage window for phased migration

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we can support both approaches depending on what the auditor prefers, but here’s how we typically handle phased migrations and what we can provide.

1) Coverage approach we provide
- Point-in-time evidence: we can export the exact configuration state (deployment manifest, instance IDs, quantization/exec flags) and traffic routing snapshot at the timestamp of cutover. That demonstrates what was running immediately before/after cutover.
- Roll-forward evidence: we can provide a short-term continuity package (24–72 hours) showing that controls (access logs, deployment approvals, monitoring alerts, change-control tickets) remained in effect across the migration.

2) What auditors usually accept
- Deployment manifests (YAML) with commit hashes tied to the cutover commit
- Audit logs showing the last successful traffic handoff, with timestamps in UTC
- KV-cache snapshot references and a small sample of request/response logs (redacted) to show no PII leakage during migration

I’m looping in Lauren (security lead on the migration) and Markus (engineering lead) to attach the timeline and the docs we normally share. We can also draft a short bridge letter that states the migration timing and which resources were in/out of scope on the cutover date.

Next steps: Lauren/Markus — can you attach the migration timeline/cutover timestamp artifacts and a quick note on what short roll-forward evidence we recommend?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Lead — Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

[Attachment referenced: bridge-letter-draft.docx (will follow)]

From: lauren_bennett <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Security - FinBank <security@finbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — coverage window for phased migration

Hi Marcus — adding the technical detail you requested and attaching the timeline. See the short checklist below and the CSV timeline attached.

Checklist for auditor evidence in phased-migration scenarios:
- Cutover timestamp (UTC) — exact moment routing changed: 2026-05-17T23:45:12Z
- Deployment manifest with commit hash + image digests for both old and new service versions (attached)
- Load balancer logs showing last tokens sent to the old instance and first tokens to new instance (we can provide 30-minute windows either side of the timestamp)
- Access control approvals and PR/merge metadata for the cutover (change ticket #RDW-4521)
- 48-hour roll-forward log slice (redacted request ids) demonstrating monitoring/alerting and no control exceptions

I attached: migration-timeline.csv (simple timeline), screenshot-snapshot-timestamps.png (control-plane UI showing the snapshot time), and a draft bridge-letter-draft.docx that you can share with your auditor.

If Pivotal Audit wants a point-in-time-only deliverable, the deployment manifest + snapshot + LB logs are usually sufficient. If they prefer roll-forward, we advise providing a short continuity package (48 hours) to show there were no control regressions immediately after cutover.

Let us know which style the auditor prefers and we’ll mark documents for that scope and produce redacted examples.

— Lauren Bennett
Security Program Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

[Attachments: migration-timeline.csv, screenshot-snapshot-timestamps.png, bridge-letter-draft.docx]

Thanks — this is helpful. We’ll discuss internally and pick one approach; two quick clarifying asks before we close the request:

1) In the bridge letter, can Redwood explicitly state the timestamp with timezone and confirm the timezone used (UTC)? That avoids ambiguity for our report.
2) For roll-forward packages: our auditor needs guaranteed redaction of any sensitive customer IDs in sample logs. Will Redwood produce redacted snippets, and can you confirm the redaction process?

If you can push an updated bridge-letter-draft.docx that includes the exact UTC timestamp and a short paragraph describing the redaction process, we’ll accept that and close the loop. We’ll use the DocuSign link you provided to finalize if needed.
